'''Jarvis Lamar Varnado''' (born March 1, 1988) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played for two seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), for the [[Boston Celtics]], [[Miami Heat]], [[Chicago Bulls]], and [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. Varnado was known as a defensive specialist and was especially adept at shot blocking, aided by his large wingspan.

==Early life==
Varnado graduated from [[Haywood High School]] in [[Brownsville, Tennessee]] in 2006.

Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Varnado was listed as the No. 16 power forward and the No. 62 player in the nation in 2006.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jarvis Varnado |url=https://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Jarvis-Varnado-40635;_ylt=AtiVKcNGYorpyBwPCCpU2jvXO5B4 |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=Rivals.yahoo.com}}</ref>

==College career==
Varnado played for [[Mississippi State Bulldogs basketball|Mississippi State]] in the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) of the [[NCAA Division I]] from 2006 to 2010.

He led the NCAA in blocks for the 2007–08 season with 157 blocks, tying [[Shaquille O'Neal]] for the most blocks in a season in the SEC. In the 2008–09 season, he would break that single season record with 170 blocks.

On November 21, 2009, Varnado became the SEC's all-time career block record holder with 413 total blocks in his career. This passed O'Neal's career block record of 412.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 21, 2009 |title=Mississippi St. 67, Bethune-Cookman 51 |url=http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=293250344 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121009172042/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=293250344 |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 9, 2012 |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> On January 23, 2010, Varnado surpassed [[Adonal Foyle]] on the NCAA's Division I all-time career blocks list to become the second-leading shot-blocker. Needing 8 blocks for the record, Varnado became the NCAA's Division I all-time shot blocker against Alabama on February 24, 2010, passing [[Wojciech Myrda]]'s record of 535 career blocks.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 24, 2010 |title=Varnado sets NCAA shot-blocking record |url=http://www.commercialappeal.com/news/2010/feb/24/mississippi-states-varnado-sets-ncaa-shot-blocking/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615173349/http://www.commercialappeal.com/news/2010/feb/24/mississippi-states-varnado-sets-ncaa-shot-blocking/ |archive-date=June 15, 2011 |access-date=February 25, 2010 |website=www.commercialappeal.com}}</ref>

Varnado was named SEC Defensive Player of the Year in 3 consecutive years (2008, 2009 and 2010) becoming the first person to do so. He is one of just two college players in history to achieve the milestone of 1,000 points, 1,000 rebounds and 500 blocks (along with [[David Robinson (basketball)|David Robinson]]).<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 6, 2013 |title=Spotted on the Pine: Jarvis Varnado |url=http://culturecrossfire.com/sports/basketball/spotted-on-the-pine-jarvis-varnado/ |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=Culturecrossfire.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==

=== Carmatic Pistoia (2010–2011) ===
Varnado was drafted by the [[Miami Heat]] with the 41st pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]]. However, he signed to play with [[Pistoia Basket 2000|Carmatic Pistoia]], an Italian team playing in the [[Serie A2 Basket|second-division]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Winderman |first=Ira |date=August 16, 2010 |title=Heat second-round pick Jarvis Varnado to play in Italy |work=Sun-Sentinel.com |url=http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2010-08-16/sports/sfl-miami-heat-jarvis-varnado-081610_1_shavlik-randolph-portland-trail-blazers-free-agent-kenny-hasbrouck |access-date=August 16, 2010 |archive-date=October 9, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101009153150/http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2010-08-16/sports/sfl-miami-heat-jarvis-varnado-081610_1_shavlik-randolph-portland-trail-blazers-free-agent-kenny-hasbrouck |url-status=dead }}</ref> Varnado played 33 games with Pistoia and averaged 15.4 points, 8.9 rebounds, and 3.1 blocks per game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Giorgio Tesi Group Pistoia basketball team – Stats |url=http://basketball.eurobasket.com/team/Italy/Giorgio_Tesi_Group_Pistoia/274?Page=3&Stats=2011 |access-date=July 28, 2012 |website=Eurobasket.com}}</ref>

=== Hapoel Jerusalem (2011–2012) ===
Varnado participated in minicamps with the Heat during the summer of 2011.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Winderman |first=Ira |date=June 27, 2011 |title=Heat minicamp includes unknowns, Eddy Curry |work=Sun-Sentinel.com |url=http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2011-06-27/sports/sfl-miami-heat-free-agent-s062711_1_dexter-pittman-heat-minicamp-d-league |access-date=July 28, 2012 |archive-date=June 30, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110630201014/http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2011-06-27/sports/sfl-miami-heat-free-agent-s062711_1_dexter-pittman-heat-minicamp-d-league |url-status=dead }}</ref> On August 12, 2011, he signed a contract with [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]] of [[Israeli Basketball Super League]]. After playing 12 games for the club in all competitions, on January 24, 2012, Varnado left the team.

=== Virtus Roma (2012) ===
After he exited Jerusalem, Varnado signed with [[Pallacanestro Virtus Roma|Virtus Roma]] of the Italian first division [[Lega Basket Serie A|Serie A]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jarvis Varnado alla Virtus Roma |url=http://www.virtusroma.it/news/ultimissime/jarvis-varnado-alla-virtus-roma/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120720122156/http://www.virtusroma.it/news/ultimissime/jarvis-varnado-alla-virtus-roma/ |archive-date=July 20, 2012 |access-date=July 28, 2012}}</ref>

=== Sioux Falls Skyforce (2012) ===
On September 7, 2012, Varnado was signed by the Heat for workouts. He was waived on October 26, 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 26, 2012 |title=HEAT Waive Carney and Varnado | Miami Heat |url=http://www.nba.com/heat/roster/heat-waive-carney-and-varnado |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> After being waived by the Heat, Varnado joined the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA Development League]]. Varnado was named D-League player of the week for the first week of the 2012–13 season.

=== Boston Celtics (2012–2013) ===
On December 24, 2012, Varnado was signed by the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 24, 2012 |title=NBA Development League: Boston Celtics Sign Sioux Falls Skyforce Center Jarvis Varnado For Year's Sixth NBA Call-Up |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/boston_celtics_sign_sioux_falls_jarvis_varnado_2012_12_24.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130105141432/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/boston_celtics_sign_sioux_falls_jarvis_varnado_2012_12_24.html |archive-date=January 5, 2013 |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 24, 2012 |title=Celtics Sign Jarvis Varnado | The Official Site of the BOSTON CELTICS |url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-sign-jarvis-varnado |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On January 6, 2013, he was waived by the Celtics.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 17, 2013 |title=Celtics Waive Joseph and Varnado | The Official Site of the BOSTON CELTICS |url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-waive-joseph-and-varnado |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

=== Miami Heat (2013) ===
On January 9, 2013, Varnado accepted a 10-day contract with the Miami Heat, the same team that drafted him in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 9, 2013 |title=HEAT Signs Jarvis Varnado | Miami Heat |url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news_recap/heat-signs-jarvis-varnado |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=NBA Development League: Sioux Falls' Jarvis Varnado Signs with the Miami Heat |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/sioux_falls_jarvis_varnado_si_2013_01_09.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140328070330/http://www.nba.com/dleague/sioux_falls_jarvis_varnado_si_2013_01_09.html |archive-date=March 28, 2014 |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He was signed to a second 10-day contract on January 20, 2013,<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 20, 2013 |title=HEAT Sign Jarvis Varnado (1/20/13) | Miami Heat |url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news_recap/heat-sign-jarvis-varnado-12013 |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> and was signed for the rest of the season on January 30.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 30, 2013 |title=HEAT Signs Jarvis Varnado | Miami Heat |url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-jarvis-varnado |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> The Heat sent him to the Sioux Falls Skyforce for assignments in March and April 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NBA Development League: 2012-13 NBA Assignments |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2012_13.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140327190108/http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2012_13.html |archive-date=March 27, 2014 |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Varnado won his first NBA championship with the Heat when they defeated the [[San Antonio Spurs]] 4–3 in the [[2013 NBA Finals]].

On October 21, 2013, Varnado was waived by the Heat.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 21, 2013 |title=HEAT Waive Varnado, Drew and Westbrook |url=http://www.nba.com/heat/heat-waive-varnado-drew-and-westbrook |access-date=October 21, 2013 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

=== Iowa Energy (2013–2014) ===
On October 31, 2013, Varnado was re-acquired by the Sioux Falls Skyforce.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 31, 2013 |title=NBA Development League: Skyforce Announces Initial 2013-14 Training Camp Invitees |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/siouxfalls/1314_training_camp_invitees_131031.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151107095620/http://www.nba.com/dleague/siouxfalls/1314_training_camp_invitees_131031.html |archive-date=November 7, 2015 |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> The next day, he was traded to the [[Iowa Wolves|Iowa Energy]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 1, 2013 |title=NBA Development League: Skyforce Acquires Draft Picks From Energy |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/siouxfalls/skyforce_energy_trade_131101.html |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On February 3, 2014, Varnado was named to the Prospects All-Star roster for the 2014 NBA D-League All-Star Game.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 3, 2014 |title=NBA Development League: Eighth Annual NBA D-League All-Star Game Features 16 Players With NBA Experience |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140207181043/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html |archive-date=February 7, 2014 |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

=== Chicago Bulls (2014) ===
On February 18, 2014, Varnado signed a 10-day contract with the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 18, 2014 |title=Bulls sign Varnado to 10-day contract | Chicago Bulls |url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-varnado-10-day-contract.html |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On February 28, 2014, the Bulls decided not to sign Varnado to a second 10-day contract.

=== Philadelphia 76ers (2014) ===
On March 1, 2014, Varnado signed a 10-day contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sixers Sign Forward Jarvis Varnado to 10-Day Contract | THE OFFICIAL SITE OF THE PHILADELPHIA 76ERS |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-sign-forward-jarvis-varnado-10-day-contract |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On March 12, 2014, he signed with the 76ers for the rest of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sixers Sign Jarvis Varnado | THE OFFICIAL SITE OF THE PHILADELPHIA 76ERS |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/140312-varnado |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On March 29, 2014, he recorded a career high 9 points and 6 blocks in a 123–98 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pistons at 76ers - March 29, 2014 - Game Preview, Play by Play, Scores and Recap on |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140329/DETPHI/gameinfo.html |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On October 7, 2014, he was waived by the 76ers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 7, 2014 |title=Sixers Sign Two Players | Philadelphia 76ers |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/141007-sixers-sign-two |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

=== Los Angeles D-Fenders (2014–2015) ===
Varnado's D-League rights were traded by the Iowa Energy to the [[South Bay Lakers|Los Angeles D-Fenders]] on December 30, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NBA Development League: D-Fenders Acquire Jarvis Varnado |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/141230_jarvisVarnado.html |access-date=December 6, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He joined the side and averaged 11.6 points in eight games.

=== Piratas de Quebradillas (2015) ===
On April 21, 2015, after the end of the 2014–15 D-League season, Varnado signed with [[Piratas de Quebradillas]] of Puerto Rico for the rest of the 2015 [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|BSN]] season.<ref>{{Cite news |date=April 21, 2015 |title=Jarvis Varnado signs with Piratas de Quebradillas |work=Sportando.com |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/158961/jarvis-varnado-signs-with-piratas-de-quebradillas.html |access-date=July 23, 2015}}</ref>

=== Dinamo Sassari (2015–2016) ===
On July 22, 2015, Varnado signed a one-year deal with [[Dinamo Basket Sassari|Dinamo Sassari]] to play in the [[Lega Basket Serie A|Serie A]] and the European first tier [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=July 22, 2015 |title=Sassari adds shot blocking ace Varnado |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/67unv4c9up7s4hmk/sassari-adds-shot-blocking-ace-varnado |access-date=July 22, 2015 |website=Euroleague.net}}</ref>

=== Istanbul Büyükşehir Belediyespor (2016–2017) ===
In July 2016, Varnado joined the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 1, 2016 |title=Lakers Announce 2016 Summer League Roster |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/160701summerleague_roster |access-date=July 1, 2016}}</ref> On August 30, 2016, Varnado was reported to have signed with [[İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyespor (basketball)|İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyespor]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|Turkish Basketball Super League]] (BSL).<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 30, 2016 |title=Jarvis Varnado signing a deal with Istanbul BSB |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/turkey/bsl/210734/jarvis-varnado-signing-a-deal-with-istanbul-bsb.html |access-date=August 30, 2016 |website=sportando.basketball |archive-date=September 4, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180904084822/https://sportando.basketball/en/turkey/bsl/210734/jarvis-varnado-signing-a-deal-with-istanbul-bsb.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> On February 5, 2017, Varnado was reported to have parted-way with [[İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyespor (basketball)|İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyespor]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 5, 2017 |title=Jarvis Varnado, Istanbul BSB part ways |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/turkey/bsl/225228/jarvis-varnado-istanbul-bsb-part-ways.html |access-date=February 5, 2017 |website=sportando.basketball |archive-date=October 5, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181005014935/https://sportando.basketball/en/turkey/bsl/225228/jarvis-varnado-istanbul-bsb-part-ways.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== Tecnyconta Zaragoza (2017–2018) ===
On August 2, 2017, Varnado was reported to have signed a one-year deal with [[Basket Zaragoza|Tecnyconta Zaragoza]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 2, 2017 |title=Zaragoza signs Jarvis Varnado |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/spain/acb/243237/zaragoza-signs-jarvis-varnado.html |access-date=August 2, 2017 |website=sportando.basketball |archive-date=October 4, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181004110047/https://sportando.basketball/en/spain/acb/243237/zaragoza-signs-jarvis-varnado.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> On March 20, 2018, Varnado was reported to have parted-way with [[Basket Zaragoza|Tecnyconta Zaragoza]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 20, 2018 |title=Jarvis Varnado, Tecnyconta Zaragoza part ways |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/spain/acb/268627/jarvis-varnado-tecnyconta-zaragoza-part-ways.html |access-date=March 20, 2018 |website=sportando.basketball |archive-date=September 4, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180904084732/https://sportando.basketball/en/spain/acb/268627/jarvis-varnado-tecnyconta-zaragoza-part-ways.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> after Varnado suffered from a plantar fascia injury in his left foot.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 7, 2018 |title=Jarvis Varnado out for two months with a left foot injury |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/spain/acb/267068/jarvis-varnado-out-for-two-months-with-a-left-foot-injury.html |access-date=March 7, 2018 |website=sportando.basketball |archive-date=September 4, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180904084717/https://sportando.basketball/en/spain/acb/267068/jarvis-varnado-out-for-two-months-with-a-left-foot-injury.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== Memphis Hustle (2018–2019) ===
On November 30, 2018, Varnado signed with the [[Memphis Hustle]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Langham |first=Geoff |date=November 30, 2018 |title=Memphis Hustle acquire Jarvis Varnado off waivers |work=NBA.com |url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-acquire-jarvis-varnado-off-waivers/ |access-date=November 30, 2018 |archive-date=December 1, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181201093217/https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-acquire-jarvis-varnado-off-waivers/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== Fos Provence (2019) ===
On January 15, 2019, Varnado parted ways with the Hustle to join [[Fos Provence Basket|Fos Provence]] of the French [[LNB Pro A]], where he averaged 9.8 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.5 blocks in 18 games played.<ref>{{Cite news |date=January 15, 2019 |title=Fos Provence signs Jarvis Varnado |work=Sportando.basketball |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/fos-provence-signs-jarvis-varnado/ |access-date=September 27, 2019 |archive-date=September 27, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190927075014/https://sportando.basketball/en/fos-provence-signs-jarvis-varnado/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== Hapoel Gilboa Galil (2019–2020) ===
On September 25, 2019, Varnado returned to Israel for a second stint, signing a one-year deal with [[Hapoel Gilboa Galil]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=September 25, 2019 |title=Gilboa Galil signs Jarvis Varnado |work=Sportando.basketball |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/gilboa-galil-signs-jarvis-varnado/ |access-date=September 25, 2019 |archive-date=September 25, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190925075625/https://sportando.basketball/en/gilboa-galil-signs-jarvis-varnado/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He averaged 7.0 points, 5.2 rebounds, and 1.2 blocks per game.<ref name="aguada" />

=== Club Atlético Aguada (2021–2023) ===
On October 6, 2021, Varnado signed with [[Club Atlético Aguada]] of the [[Liga Uruguaya de Básquetbol]].<ref name="aguada">{{cite web |title=Aguada tabs Jarvis Varnado, ex H.Galil Gilboa |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Israel/news/707769/Aguada-tabs-Jarvis-Varnado,-ex-H.Galil-Gilboa |website=Eurobasket |access-date=October 6, 2021 |date=October 6, 2021}}</ref>
